Theme

Travel & transport · Household, washing & chores

fuel noun

also fuels, firewood, fuel for the fire, fuel tank, diesel, diesel fuel

classical

Ov. Met. 14.532: alimentaque cētera flammae (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 14.5: alimentīs ignium (Lewis & Short, s.v. molestus)

alimentum, alimentī n.

noun, second declension

fuel (of a fire); food

Its first sense is food, nourishment; for fuel it takes a genitive, ignis or flammae, and in the poets is always plural (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens (s.v. fuel) has the plural for the fuel of machines too (Egger).

Other words

  • lignum, lignī n. — firewood (in the plural)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 2.17.26: suggerunt affatim ligna proximae silvae; Varro LL 6.66

    The household fuel: ligna are logs for the fire, as against māteria, timber for building (Lewis & Short, s.v. māteria). See wood.

  • māteria prōpulsōria, māteriae prōpulsōriae f. — fuel (for engines)

    also used · modern · Traupman 216, 319

    Traupman’s phrase; Egger has liquor prōpulsōrius (M-O s.v. fuel). For a car, petrol is benzīnum (see petrol).

  • fōmes, fōmitis m. — kindling, tinder

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.176 (Lewis & Short)

    Dry stuff to catch a spark; in Christian Latin, figuratively, the tinder of sin.

Examples

  • picem et cērās, alimentaque cētera flammae

    pitch and wax and everything else that feeds a flameOv. Met. 14.532 (Lewis & Short)

  • suggerunt affatim ligna proximae silvae

    the nearby woods supply plenty of firewoodPlin. Ep. 2.17.26

  • Dīseliānum benzīnum

    diesel fuelTraupman 216

See also petrol, wood, fire, engine, kindle a fire, tank.
